research-record.title: Growing the doc-tool prose document classes

banner.note: Status: proposal for owner review — a design pass, not a decision record (gandr-712, phase B). It records the class designs, the treefmt/policy cutover, and the decisions held for owner veto.

Scope: grow the doc tool (gandr-workflow-docs, gandr-fcw.8) beyond the docs/spec component corpus to the surrounding Markdown tail, so the markdown-to-XML convergence can cut over and the .md tail stops growing. No existing .md file is migrated in this lane; the appendix prices that later sweep.
Dogfood: this record is itself the first instance of the research-record class, authored as XML and validated by the tool it designs (check-docs). The bootstrap is the acceptance test.

section.title: What this lane grows
section.prose: The doc tool already owns one document class: the component spec vocabulary under docs/spec , where parsing is validation. Everything outside docs/spec still authors as Markdown because no XML class existed for it. This lane grows the three missing classes so the authoring policy can turn XML-first.

The classes share one minimal block and inline substrate and differ only in their banner obligation, their root attributes, and whether they may coin cross-referenced labels. The canonical formatter is class-agnostic, so no formatting code is added — only the docs-xml treefmt globs widen to the new roots (
).

list.item: docs/research/*.xml — design studies and staging records: a status banner, sections, tables, code, coined-label anchors, and register-key citations.
docs/workflow/*.xml — process and convention docs: a required read-when banner and rule/convention lists.
crates/*/docs/STATUS.xml — the crate status narrative: a crate scope, dated sections, current-state prose. Kept deliberately minimal; off the corpus main-path by design.

section.title: The shared substrate
section.prose:
All three classes are configurations of one substrate. The block vocabulary is the minimum each class needs; it omits the component corpus's math-bearing blocks (judgements, grammar, rule, diagram), which prose documents do not carry. The inline label and ref anchors are admitted only in a research-record (
).

section.title: Design decisions
section.prose: Each decision below is a coined anchor; the ones held for owner veto are gathered in the next section.

list.item: R1 — reuse the component Status enum for the doc family rather than mint a research-specific status enum. The five spellings map cleanly (a design study or proposal is design-pass ; adopted is adopted-unbuilt / built ; retired is dormant ), which keeps one status concept across both corpora. Cost: the machine status is coarser than the banner's human phrase, so the phrase lives in the banner.

R2 — one shared substrate with a per-class schema, not three parallel model/parse/validate stacks. The classes differ by banner obligation and admitted inlines, expressed as a small schema, so a bug fixed once is fixed for all three and the vocabulary stays minimal. The component stack is left untouched: a prose document is a distinct root element, so the two corpora coexist.

R3 — coined labels ( label / ref ) are a research-record affordance only. The recommendation/hazard/question anchor is a design-study device; a workflow or crate-status document that coins one is a schema violation ( disallowed-inline ). This is the one real per-class inline restriction; the block set is otherwise shared.

D1 — recommend the per-crate CHANGELOG class DIE rather than migrate. See the owner-veto section: the changelog is prose with near-zero validatable structure, better served by folding into STATUS plus beads and git history.

section.title: Decisions for owner-veto review
section.prose: Separated from the recommendations above; each is a genuine fork the owner decides at review.

list.item:
O1 — class root names and the per-crate file layout. The roots are research-record , workflow-doc , crate-status ; the per-crate file is proposed as crates/*/docs/STATUS.xml beside the retiring STATUS.md . Ratify the names and whether a per-crate CHANGELOG gets its own root or is subsumed (see
).

O3 — the block set is currently shared across all three classes (only the
inline restriction distinguishes them). Confirm this is right, or name a per-class block restriction (for example, tables in the lean tier) worth enforcing. Recommendation: keep the block set shared; premature per-class block restrictions are the expensive wrong-early-vocabulary the charter warns against.

O4 — cross-document references (a research record pointing at another doc's section) are modeled as prose plus inline-code , not a resolved see element. Resolving them corpus-wide is a growth point deferred to the static-HTML render target. Confirm deferral.

section.title: Dogfood outcome
section.prose:
One vocabulary judgement surfaced while authoring and is recorded honestly: nested lists (sub-bullets) are not in the minimal substrate — a list is flat. The research and workflow tails use sub-bullets, so nesting is a likely early growth point; it was left out to keep the first vocabulary minimal and to avoid a second recursion axis in the parser. Flag, not fix (
is the review hook).
